Defensible space · canopy model comparison · local draft, not published

CHMv2 vs CHMv1 national comparison · 2026-10-19

195 of 1,172 1° tiles finished by the national CHMv2 run (snapshot 2026-10-19 16:19 UTC) · 82,872,173 US structures, 46% of the national total · ring canopy (CHMv1 fp16 as in the paper, CHMv1 fp32, CHMv2) and the modelled effect of clearing it, paper map vs proposed map, nationally and by ecoregion, state and county

By Carlo Broderick, NCEAS, UC Santa Barbara · 2026-10-19 09:54 PDT

Is the national map different if the paper's canopy model (CHMv1) is swapped for CHMv2? This page compares the two on every structure the CHMv2 run has finished so far.

How to read this page

One structure = one building footprint. Ring canopy = share of the 0–100 ft ring around it (footprint removed) where the canopy model predicts trees ≥ 1 m tall. CHMv1 = the canopy model in the submitted paper (Meta HighResCanopyHeight, run in half precision); CHMv2 = Meta's newer CHMv2 model on 0.6 m NAIP. The paper map scores each structure with the paper's model; the proposed map uses CHMv2 canopy with the model refitted on CHMv2. "Clearing helps / hurts" = clearing the ring lowers / raises the modelled loss probability by more than 5 points; shares are of scored structures (canopy above zero), as in the paper. Hover or tap any bar, cell or county for counts; maps have layer buttons.

Bottom line

Canopy: a small change in level, the same geography. On the 79,668,210 US structures compared so far, CHMv2 reads +2.0 points more ring canopy than the paper's CHMv1 on average (24.0% → 25.9%). Structure by structure the two correlate at 0.92, and counties keep their order (rank correlation 0.95). The biggest systematic change: CHMv1 read 13% of rings as exactly bare, CHMv2 only 0.9%. CHMv2 is higher in the arid West and California and lower in leafy eastern and midwestern states.

Clearing map: a substantial change in the West, a small one in the East. Among scored structures, the share where clearing the ring helps goes from 26.4% on the paper map to 34.8% on the proposed map (+8.4 points); hurts stays at 27.2% → 27.2% and neutral moves -8.3 points. 21% of structures scored on both maps change class. About 54% of the national shift appears with CHMv2 canopy alone in the paper's model; the rest comes from the refitted model. The Carlson-fire cohort moved 55% → 72%; nationally the move is about half as large, but California's Mixed/Mediterranean region moves almost as much as the cohort.

  • Forest: helps 23% → 24% (+2 points; CHMv2 canopy through the paper model alone: 23%); mean canopy +0.2 points
  • Mixed/Mediterranean: helps 53% → 69% (+16 points; CHMv2 canopy through the paper model alone: 81%); mean canopy +7.6 points
  • Grass/Shrub/Desert: helps 24% → 45% (+21 points; CHMv2 canopy through the paper model alone: 20%); mean canopy +4.1 points

Largest state shifts in the share helped: CO +45, UT +32, OK +29, TX +26, MO +26, KS +22 points (Plains and interior West states, driven by the refitted Grass/Shrub/Desert terms). CHMv2 reads less canopy than CHMv1 in KS (-7.5), WI (-6.1), MI (-5.3), MN (-4.8), MO (-4.3), AL (-3.9), DC (-3.2), NH (-3.1), MA (-2.6), VT (-2.4), GA (-2.3), NC (-2.0), CT (-1.7), OH (-1.0), MS (-0.7), KY (-0.7), IL (-0.6) points.

These are the 195 tiles finished so far (46% of national structures, California and eastern metros first); the rural interior West, Rockies and Plains are not in yet (only their metros are). Reweighted to the paper's national ecoregion mix, the national share helped would move from about 32% to about 39%: a direction, not a number.

How this panel was checked
  • Join on building_id (string) per tile; IDs cast to string when a file stores them otherwise; duplicates dropped (none found).
  • The paper map is reproduced exactly: 195 of 195 tiles give the paper's help / neutral / hurt counts to the structure.

Rings left out, and rings reading exactly zero

CHMv1 in half precision (fp16), as used in the paper, could not read 23% of the ring pixels that the full-precision run reads, so more rings had nothing valid. CHMv2 leaves out fewer rings and almost never reads exactly zero.Valid ring area share: fp16 47.7%, fp32 61.6%, CHMv2 62.3% (CHMv2 additionally removes 22.2% of ring area with NDVI < 0 as observed non-tree). CHMv1 writes unobserved rings as 0.0 (3,097,632 such US rings here); the paper's scoring drops them via chm_validpx_ring100ft > 0, as here.

2 · How different is the canopy?

Canopy here is the share of the 0–100 ft ring around each structure (footprint removed) with predicted tree height of at least 1 m. Δ = CHMv2 − CHMv1 (paper, fp16) in percentage points.

Per-structure difference, CHMv2 minus CHMv1

Most structures land within a few points of each other: half are between -3 and +8 points, and 90% between -15 and +16. CHMv2 reads higher on 64% of structures and lower on 35%.n = 79,668,210 US structures valid in both (outside-US structures excluded). Mean +1.98 pts, median +3, mean |Δ| 7.6 pts, Pearson r 0.924. Tails beyond ±40 points pooled into the end bins.

4 · Does the clearing map change?

Each structure is scored as the paper does: the modelled probability of loss with its observed ring canopy minus the probability with the ring cleared. 'Clearing helps' means clearing lowers the modelled loss probability by more than 5 percentage points.

Where clearing the ring helps, is neutral or hurts: US structures compared so far

Paper map: clearing helps 26.4% (18,269,323 of 69,076,391). Proposed map: 34.8% (28,130,299 of 80,746,622). The proposed map scores more structures (80,746,622 vs 69,076,391) because CHMv2 reads exactly zero canopy far less often. On the 68,933,347 structures scored on both maps the shares are 26.5% → 38.4% helped and 27.3% → 31.1% hurt.Classifier as Cat Fong's 08_score_national.R: Δp = p(observed canopy) − p(canopy = 0) from the logit GLM destroyed ~ veg × structures × ecoregion_broad + CWD; helps if Δp > 0.05, hurts if Δp < −0.05, neutral otherwise; canopy = chm_ge1m_frac_ring100ft where chm_validpx_ring100ft > 0; denominator = scored (canopy > 0 with CWD and ecoregion). Structures = stage-2 struct_count_200m; CWD = TerraClimate 2025 annual; ecoregion = dissolved EPA L1. Paper model = glm_3x3_ge1m.rds; proposed = refit on veg_chmv2_native06 (same 192,754 Carlson structures; coefficients verified against the Carlson refit).

5 · How representative is this, and what would the national number be?

The finished tiles against the whole country

The CHMv2 run went California first, then eastern and midwestern metros by size, so the finished tiles are not a random sample. They hold 46% of national structures but are denser and leafier than the country as a whole.

Indicative national estimate (with a strong caveat)

Taking the change seen in each ecoregion in the finished tiles and applying it to the paper's national ecoregion mix, the national share where clearing helps would go from about 32% to about 39%. the rural interior West, Rockies and Plains are not yet run, so treat this as a direction, not a number.Estimate = paper national share + Σ_eco w_eco × (share_B,eco − share_A,eco), w_eco = the ecoregion's share of the paper's nationally scored structures; shifts measured on US structures in the finished tiles. Assumes the within-ecoregion shift in unfinished tiles equals the finished-tile shift; scored populations differ between maps (CHMv2 scores more structures).

Paper nationalEcoregion-weighted change (proposed − paper)Indicative national, proposed mapInput-only (CHMv2 canopy, paper model)
Clearing helps32.1%+6.538.6%33.3%
Clearing hurts21.4%+2.223.5%23.6%

Caveats, plainly

  • Partial coverage. 195 of 1,172 tiles with structures, 46% of national structures; California and eastern metros are over-represented; the rural interior West, Rockies and Plains are missing (their metros are in).
  • fp16 vs fp32. The paper's CHMv1 numbers were run in half precision, which could not read about 23% of ring pixels; these void pixels count as non-canopy. The full-precision CHMv1 re-run differs from the paper run by -1.2 points of mean canopy here, and moves the share helped -0.9 points, so voiding is not what separates CHMv1 from CHMv2.
  • TF32. 86 tiles were run with TF32 matrix maths, 95 in plain fp32 (14 early tiles did not record it); a dedicated test found the two equivalent for this purpose.
  • 1 m NAIP pockets. Where CHMv2 had only older 1 m NAIP (289,377 compared structures), the planned 1 m height correction has not been applied.
  • Same model form, new fit. The proposed map uses a model refitted on CHMv2 canopy for the same Carlson fires; model uncertainty is not shown here.
  • Census not sample. These are all structures in the finished tiles, so there is no sampling error, but the tiles themselves are not a random draw.

Sources

  • Building footprints: Overture Maps Foundation buildings (internal national product, stage 1).
  • Canopy: Meta HighResCanopyHeight (CHMv1; Tolan et al. 2024) and Meta CHMv2 (facebook/dinov3-vitl16-chmv2-dpt-head), both on USDA NAIP imagery via Microsoft Planetary Computer.
  • Climatic water deficit: TerraClimate 2025 (Abatzoglou et al. 2018). Ecoregions: US EPA Level I, dissolved to three broad classes.
  • Model: the paper's logit GLM on the Carlson destroyed/damaged structure set (Fong et al., in review) and its CHMv2 refit.
  • County and state boundaries: US Census Bureau 2020 cartographic boundary files (1:500k).
